# SB-1030 Safety bulletin: quench oil fire risk

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P2, line P2-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L1-RR01

Hazard description
- Summary: A quench oil fire hazard has been identified associated with radial ring rolling operations on EQ-P2-L1-RR01. The hazard originates from oil contacting hot surfaces or sparks during upset conditions and from inadequate containment or retention at the quench interface. A fire can propagate rapidly if oil is atomized onto a hot workpiece or bearing housing. This bulletin describes contributing factors observed during a recent incident review, the underlying mechanisms, and the risk control measures required to mitigate the fire potential.
- Background and mechanism: During radial ring rolling, excess quench oil at the mandrel or roll interface can be entrained and dispersed under the influence of centrifugal forces or mechanical impact. When dispersed into fine droplets, oil has a much greater tendency to ignite if it contacts a hot metal surface or a persistent ignition source such as a bearing failure that generates hot particles. Contamination of oil with metal particles or degraded oil increases flash propensity. Oil leaks that travel along machine frames can bypass standard drip trays and enter cavities near high-temperature zones. Lack of effective oil containment or misadjusted clamps can allow oil to reach the mandrel bearing and chuck surfaces.
- Contributing human and systems factors: Inadequate pre-shift inspection, incomplete housekeeping of drip trays, use of oil with increased particulate load, and incorrect tightening of critical clamp fasteners were observed as recurring issues. Maintenance documentation review showed varying practice in mandrel clamp maintenance; this bulletin standardizes the control point for clamp bolt torque for EQ-P2-L1-RR01 and clarifies where records must be kept.

Affected equipment
- Scope: All radial ring rolling operations performed on EQ-P2-L1-RR01 located on P2-L1 are affected. Special attention is required for the mandrel clamp assembly and adjacent quench delivery plumbing and containment, including external drip trays and local shielding.
- Components of concern: Mandrel clamp assembly, quench nozzles at the mandrel face, drip containment pans that route toward bearing housings, and heat-affected zones on adjacent roll housings. Operators and maintenance personnel working on or near these components must follow the controls in this bulletin.

Required controls
- Tightening control: The mandrel clamp bolt torque for Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L1-RR01) is 430 N·m. This torque value is the authorized setting for the clamp bolt. Use a calibrated torque device and follow the procedure steps in SOP-P2-L1-04 when applying torque. Record the torque value in the clamp maintenance log each time the clamp is reassembled.
- Pre-shift and pre-start inspections: Verify quench nozzles are positioned and secured, drip trays are clean and free-flow paths are not blocked, and visual oil leaks are absent along the quench feed lines and mandrel housing. If any oil accumulation is observed on or near hot surfaces, remove oil, clean the area, and escalate to maintenance before starting production.
- Quench delivery and containment: Ensure quench returns are routed to dedicated containment rather than machine frame cavities. Fit and maintain splash shields at the quench-to-mandrel interface that direct any overflow to the containment pan. Where splash shields are absent or damaged, tag the machine out of service until repairs are completed per MM-P2-L1-RR01-S2.
- Oil condition and filtration: Do not operate with visibly degraded oil or oil containing metal particulates. Replace or filter oil according to SOP-P2-L1-05 and document oil change or filtration actions in the quench system maintenance record.
- Hot condition response: If a hot workpiece or hot bearing condition is suspected, stop the machine and allow the area to cool per SOP-P2-L1-04 procedures before attempting any oil removal. If oil contact with a hot surface occurs, follow the emergency isolation and fire response steps in the local emergency plan and report the event to line management.
- Housekeeping and training: Maintain clean drip trays and surrounding floor areas. Train operators on recognizing signs of oil atomization and the specific consequences of splash onto hot surfaces. Include the clamp torque requirement and quench routing checks in toolbox talks and training records.
- Verification and audits: Maintenance must audit clamp bolt torque on reassembly and include torque entries in the clamp maintenance log. Production leads must verify pre-shift inspections are performed and documented on the pre-start checklist. The safety team will perform periodic verification audits against MM-P2-L1-RR01-S2 to confirm compliance.

Rationale and examples
- Rationale for torque control: Proper clamp bolt torque ensures consistent clamp engagement and minimizes relative movement at the mandrel face that can create pathways for oil to be forced or wicked into critical zones. Inconsistent clamp preload can lead to micro-gaps that permit oil migration under pressure or during dynamic loading.
- Examples:
  - Example A: A clamp reassembled without specified torque permitted axial play under load; subsequent quench overflow migrated into the bearing housing and resulted in smoke during a production run. The root cause included no torque record and a missing splash shield.
  - Example B: Clean drip trays and correctly routed returns captured a quench overflow event and prevented oil reaching hot surfaces; the event was documented and repairs were made with zero fire escalation.

Records to keep
- Clamp maintenance log: Record each clamp disassembly/reassembly, including the mandrel clamp bolt torque set to 430 N·m and the calibration identifier of the torque device used.
- Pre-start checklist: Document completion of the quench nozzle, drip tray, and leak inspections before each production start per SOP-P2-L1-04.
- Oil service and filter log: Record oil changes, filtration events, and contamination findings as required by SOP-P2-L1-05.
- Incident and audit reports: File any near-miss or incident reports and the results of verification audits per MM-P2-L1-RR01-S2.

Related documents
- MM-P2-L1-RR01-S2
- SOP-P2-L1-04
- SOP-P2-L1-05

Effective date
- Effective immediately upon issuance of Revision Rev C. All controls in this bulletin are mandatory and must be implemented and documented as described above.
